text.en:
Pooja travelled by train from Chennai to Delhi. At each station people spoke a different language and wore different clothes.
A co-passenger shared rotis and she shared curd rice.
"We look different but we eat together and smile together," she said.

India has hundreds of languages. The Constitution lists 22 major languages such as Tamil, Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi and Urdu. Many people speak more than one language.
Dress and food change with climate and region. People in the cold north wear woollen clothes, while people in the hot south often wear light cotton. Rice is common in the east and south, and wheat rotis in the north.
In spite of these differences we are one country. This is unity in diversity.
India has hundreds of languages. Tamil, Hindi, Bengali and Telugu are some.
Dress and food change with the climate of each region.
The north has woollen clothes and wheat rotis. The south has cotton and rice.
We look different but we are one country. This is unity in diversity.

problem.en: Why do people in cold hills wear woollen clothes while people on the hot coast wear cotton?

text.en: Hills are cold, so wool keeps the body warm.
The coast is hot and humid, so light cotton is comfortable.
So dress depends on climate and region.

prompt.en: A friend says one language is enough for the whole country. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: India has many languages, each with its own culture.
Knowing several languages helps us understand each other.

points.en: Food and dress change with region and climate.
We are one country in spite of differences.
